sentence: To find the sum of \(\frac{1}{n}\) over all positive integers \(n\) such that the decimal representation of \(\frac{1}{n}\) terminates, we first need to understand under what conditions \(\frac{1}{n}\) is a terminating decimal.
sentence-category-reason: States the goal and declares the immediate approach to determine when 1/n terminates.

sentence: A fraction \(\frac{1}{n}\) has a terminating decimal representation if and only if the denominator \(n\), in its simplest form, has only the prime factors 2 and/or 5.
sentence-category-reason: Recalls the characterization of denominators that yield terminating decimals.

sentence: This is because a fraction has a terminating decimal if and only if its denominator divides some power of 10, and 10 itself has the prime factors 2 and 5 only.
sentence-category-reason: Explains why the condition holds using properties of powers of 10.

sentence:
Thus, any positive integer \(n\) that results in \(\frac{1}{n}\) as a terminating decimal can be expressed in the form: \[
n = 2^a \times 5^b
\]
sentence-category-reason: Deduces the form of n based on the terminating condition.
Clarifies the parameters in the deduced form of n.
Sets up the actual summation over all qualifying n as a double series.

sentence:
We can split this sum into the product of two geometric series: \[
\left( \sum_{a=0}^{\infty} \frac{1}{2^a} \right) \times \left( \sum_{b=0}^{\infty} \frac{1}{5^b} \right)
\]
sentence-category-reason: Carries out the decomposition of the double sum into a product of two geometric series.
Computes the first geometric series explicitly.
Computes the second geometric series explicitly.
Multiplies the two series sums to obtain the total.
